summary: fdump_end_frame() reads the display surface straight out of guest VRAM (dump_surface_ppm -> d->vram_ptr + surface->vram_addr, renderer.c:458, with no draw_dirty test and no download), on the stated ground that 'the flip's own pgraph_vk_finish' has already put it there. It has not. pgraph_vk_prerecord_display_download() (surface.c:1395-1450) only RECORDS the copy into the aux command buffer and sets display_predownload_pending; the staging->VRAM memcpy lives solely in pgraph_vk_complete_staged_downloads() (surface.c:636-697). VK_FINISH_REASON_FLIP_STALL is in the deferred set (draw.c:3331-3334) and flip_stall is not render-thread context, so the finish takes the else branch at draw.c:3400, spin-waits only on frame_submitted[] (vkQueueSubmit issued, fence not signalled) and skips both complete_staged_downloads() calls, which are inside if (!deferred) at draw.c:3391 and draw.c:3457. The frame-rotation block at draw.c:3494-3530 completes only if deferred_downloads_frame == next_frame, and the download was recorded into current_frame. Nothing between renderer.c:2049 and renderer.c:2258 completes it either. So every per-frame PPM holds the most recently COMPLETED download, not this frame's.
scenario: A soak arms --env XEMU_FRAME_DUMP=30,after120 on a normal 3D title, so the display surface is draw_dirty at every flip and prerecord_display_download() returns true each time. For flip N the dump writes framedump_<id>_f0NN.ppm from VRAM, which still holds frame N-1 in the steady state (the completion happens later, on the display thread's get_framebuffer_surface -> wait_for_surface_download -> process_pending_downloads path, surface.c:1455-1477) and older whenever the display thread has not presented since. The frame record on the same line carries "f": N, this frame's draws, this frame's submits_in_frame and this frame's nv2a_frame. Nothing in the artifact says the image is not frame N's. #77's method is to pick from the PPMs which of 30 frames show the deck/ground stipple and then read those frames' draw records, so a shift that is at least one frame and is not even constant assigns the artifact's draw state to its neighbour. The failure is silent -- a one-frame-old display surface is a completely plausible picture -- and the PR's published evidence (30 distinct nv2a_frame values, 3,847 draws) is all read from the records, not the images, so the measured run could not have caught it. The codebase has paid for this pipeline once already: surface.c:679-686 records that crediting a pre-recorded display download with the current generation 'made the surface clean with VRAM one draw behind' and that Depth buffer fixed function came back as the clear and no quad in one run out of three depending on where the flip fell.
remediation: A REMEDIATION IS A CLAIM, and the obvious fix costs the instrument its headline property, so the lane should pick rather than be told. (a) Call pgraph_vk_download_surface_complete_deferred(d) at the top of fdump_end_frame() inside if (fdump.images): it waits frame_fences[display_predownload_frame_index] and memcpys -- one fence wait per FRAME, at the flip, where a stall already lives, and none at all under noimages. It adds synchronisation the current comment promises not to add, so the comment and the session header must stop claiming otherwise; it adds no per-draw finish, so cb_draws/submits should be re-measured rather than assumed unchanged. (b) File the PPM against the PREVIOUS frame record, which is the frame it actually holds, carrying that record's f and nv2a_frame into the image name so the pairing is in the artifact. (c) Default images off and move 'no trustworthy per-frame picture' into the WHAT IT CANNOT SEE list. Whichever is chosen, renderer.c:1947-1949, docs/lanes/diagdump77/NOTES.md:47-49, the PR body and the AGENTS.md section must stop asserting the surface is already in VRAM. PASS 2 SHOULD CHECK THE MECHANISM, NOT THE WORDS: that the image written for frame N is produced after a completion naming frame N's fence, or that the record it is filed under is the one whose pixels it holds.
evidence: renderer.c:1947-1949 (the comment), renderer.c:1950-1975 (fdump_end_frame), renderer.c:458-462 (dump_surface_ppm reads vram_ptr directly and reports failure only through DIAG_LOG). renderer.c:2047 (prerecord call), renderer.c:2049 (the FLIP_STALL finish), renderer.c:2254-2260 (the new fdump hooks). surface.c:1395-1450 (prerecord records only), surface.c:636-697 (the only staging->VRAM memcpy), surface.c:700-763 (download_surface_complete_deferred, the wait+complete pair), surface.c:1455-1477 (the Android force-download present path). draw.c:3331-3334 (deferred set includes FLIP_STALL), draw.c:3340 (render-thread branch, not taken here), draw.c:3391 and draw.c:3457 (both completions inside if (!deferred)), draw.c:3443-3448 (the spin-wait is on frame_submitted, not the fence), draw.c:3494-3530 (rotation completes only for next_frame). Not device-verified: this is a code-path argument, stated as one.

summary: fdump_base_dir() ends `return xemu_settings_get_base_path();`, which on Android is SDL_GetPrefPath("xemu","xemu") -- internal storage (ui/xemu-settings.cc:77-91). That is precisely the fallback the Android entry point says it refuses: xemu_android.cpp:1132-1136 states 'Internal storage is NOT a fallback here ... better to leave the feature unarmed and say so', and its failing branch logs a WARN and leaves fdump_dir empty. Empty fdump_dir does not leave the feature unarmed; it arms it into the directory the comment names as unusable.
scenario: A dispatched soak runs --env XEMU_FRAME_DUMP=30,after120 on a device where SDL_AndroidGetExternalStorageState() does not report WRITE -- the same condition the TB-cache block two lines below (xemu_android.cpp:1154-1157) treats as reachable enough to code its own fallback for. One WARN goes to logcat at startup, 120 s before anything happens. The env arm then fires normally: fdump_begin() opens the jsonl under internal storage and FDUMP_LOG prints 'framedump: armed by env, 30 frames, images=1, cap=96 MB -> <path>' at WARN -- a success line naming a path nobody can reach -- and 30 records plus ~27 MB of PPMs are written where --pull 'framedump_*' cannot see them. The run returns no dump and a log saying one was written. The marker branch is harmlessly inert in the same state (nobody can drop a marker there either), which is what makes this easy to miss: only the env arm reaches it.
remediation: Give the Android path an explicit unarmed state instead of letting it fall through: under __ANDROID__ make nv2a_dbg_set_framedump_dir() the only way the feature turns on, and have fdump_poll_marker() return early with a one-time WARN when fdump_dir is empty on that platform. Keep the settings-base-path fallback for desktop, where it is the right answer and is documented as such. Do NOT fix this by aiming the Android fallback at internal storage deliberately -- the comment's reasoning is correct and a dump nobody can pull is worse than no dump.
evidence: renderer.c:1573-1583 (fdump_base_dir), renderer.c:1578-1580 (the fdump_dir branch), renderer.c:1582 (the fallback). android/app/src/main/cpp/xemu_android.cpp:1126-1147 (the comment and both branches). ui/xemu-settings.cc:77-91 (base path is SDL_GetPrefPath). renderer.c:1817-1824 (the env arm, which fires regardless of where the directory points) and renderer.c:1755-1757 (the FDUMP_LOG success line).

summary: `if max_cb <= 1:` is the whole SERIALISED test and it has no minimum-sample guard. The PR's own measurement says cb_draws == 1 occurs in the LIVE arm at the first draw of every frame (the flip's own finish), so any correct live dump whose frames carry one draw each satisfies the serialised test exactly -- and the submits test degrades with it, because one draw and one flip submission per frame gives 1.0000 submits per draw. The two columns the docstring calls 'two independent readings of the same fact' are not independent at low draw counts, which is the case where a verdict is least warranted. The header-vs-records disagreement check then fires on top, telling the reader to treat a correct dump's provenance as unreliable.
scenario: REPRODUCED against the unmodified checker. Built a dump with per_draw_finish=false, also_diag=false, 30 frames, one cb_draws=1 draw per frame and one submit per frame; framedump_check.py printed 'cb_draws max=1 distribution={1: 30}', 'submits median 1.0000 per draw', 'SERIALISED: no command buffer ever held more than one draw', 'SERIALISED by submits', and 'INSTRUMENT DISAGREES WITH ITSELF ... treat this dump's provenance as unreliable until that is explained', exit 1. afterNN exists precisely because a queued soak cannot choose its moment, so an arm that lands on a loading screen, a pause menu, a video cut or the tail of a title that has stopped issuing geometry produces this dump -- and the reader gets a confident falsification of the PR's entire thesis from an instrument that behaved correctly. The selftest cannot catch it: write_dump() hard-codes draws=40 and never varies it.
remediation: Refuse the verdict rather than inverting it. Compute draws per frame and, below a threshold (a handful per frame, or fewer than some tens of draws in total), print 'INSUFFICIENT SAMPLE: N draws over M frames cannot distinguish the two paths -- a per-draw finish is indistinguishable from a frame that only drew once' and return a status distinct from both verdicts; suppress the header-vs-records disagreement check in that state for the same reason. Add a selftest case with draws=1 asserting the insufficient-sample branch, since the whole argument for this checker is that its verdicts have been made to fire deliberately.
evidence: framedump_check.py:129-140 (the cb_draws verdict), :142-150 (the submits verdict), :158-170 (the disagreement check), :104 (max_cb). framedump_check_selftest.py:24-26 (write_dump signature, draws=40 fixed) and :70-113 (no low-draw case). The PR body's own line: 'cb_draws == 1 occurs in the live arm exactly 30 times in 3,847 draws, and that set is exactly the first draw of each frame'.

summary: fdump_begin() passes the dump's frame count straight to nv2a_dbg_trigger_diag_frames(frames), but the two count different things. `frames` counts flip_stall invocations -- that is what fdump_end_frame() decrements, and this lane established the distinction itself in AGENTS.md and commit 7fa7d27047. nv2a_dbg_trigger_diag_frames() counts GUEST frames: the diag session advances on diag_frame_num = g_nv2a_stats.frame_count (renderer.c:2224, :2244). The PR's own control-arm table is the measurement that these are not the same number: 30 frame records, 1 distinct guest frame.
scenario: A soak arms --env XEMU_FRAME_DUMP=30,after120,diag. The live dump closes after 30 flip_stalls -- by the lane's measurement about one second of wall clock, still inside guest frame 3127. The diag capture was asked for 30 GUEST frames and has completed one. It keeps running, with its pgraph_vk_finish before every draw and its per-frame surface readbacks, for as long as the frozen title needs to advance 29 more guest frames, with nothing recording it and nothing the operator typed bounding it; at the measured stall factor that is on the order of 900 flip_stalls. Every other measurement that soak was queued for -- frame timing, the artifact rate, soak_title.sh's own logs -- is then taken under a serialising capture the spec said would last 30 frames. DIAG_MAX_FRAMES is 64 (renderer.c:502) and nv2a_dbg_trigger_diag_frames() clamps before diag_init_session() sizes anything, so there is no overrun and no crash: the clamp bounds the diag session's arrays, not its duration.
remediation: Either scale the control arm to the unit the operator typed -- pass an explicitly documented guest-frame count rather than `frames` -- or close the diag capture when the dump closes, tearing down from fdump_close() when the dump is what armed it. The second is the better shape because it makes 'the control arm is the dump's control' true by construction rather than by arithmetic the operator has to do. If neither is taken, the spec comment at renderer.c:1638-1640 must say that diag does not end when the dump does.
evidence: renderer.c:1760-1763 (the pass-through), renderer.c:1993-2001 (fdump_end_frame decrements frames_remaining per flip_stall), renderer.c:561-568 (trigger_diag_frames and its DIAG_MAX_FRAMES clamp), renderer.c:502 (DIAG_MAX_FRAMES 64), renderer.c:2224 and :2244 (diag_frame_num from g_nv2a_stats.frame_count). The PR body's control-arm table: 30 frame records, 1 distinct guest frame (3127, all thirty). AGENTS.md's new note: 'A frame record is one flip_stall, not one guest frame.'

summary: A failed per-frame PPM write is announced only through DIAG_LOG / hakuX-diag (renderer.c:462) -- the tag this PR's own commit ad5d93f489 established is absent from both logcat specs that serve a dispatched run. dump_surface_ppm() also returns silently when surface->fmt.bytes_per_pixel is 0, which the caller's `disp->width && disp->height` test does not cover. Either way fdump_end_frame() has already committed `image` to the frame record and has already charged iw*ih*3 bytes to the cap, so the dump names a file that is not there and shortens itself for a write that did not happen, with nothing in the run's log.
scenario: External storage fills mid-dump, or the directory is the M1 one. From frame k onward every PPM fopen fails; the jsonl keeps emitting "image":"framedump_<id>_fNNN.ppm" and keeps adding ~900 KB per frame to bytes_written, so the byte cap closes the dump early for bytes never written. The reader pulls the run, finds records naming images that do not exist, and has no line on any kept tag to explain it -- the same invisibility this lane fixed for its own lifecycle lines and did not extend to the one call those lines depend on.
remediation: Report through FDUMP_LOG when dump_surface_ppm() is called from this path (or give it a return value), emit "image": null on failure, and only charge the cap for bytes actually written.
evidence: renderer.c:446-488 (dump_surface_ppm; :454-456 the silent bpp return, :462 the DIAG_LOG), renderer.c:1960-1972 (the caller, image name and byte charge). The lane's own commit ad5d93f489 and the comment at renderer.c:1591-1601 naming dispatcher.sh:1089 and soak_title.sh:32.

summary: The WARN covers only the SDL_AndroidGetExternalStorageState() branch. If the state reports WRITE but SDL_AndroidGetExternalStoragePath() returns NULL or "", the inner `if (files_dir && files_dir[0])` fails and the run produces no line on any tag at all.
scenario: Storage state says writable, the path query fails; the operator sees neither the 'marker <dir>/frame_dump.on' INFO nor the 'no writable external storage' WARN, and the dump is silently unarmed -- or, with M1, silently armed into internal storage.
remediation: One else covering both failures, with the same WARN text.

summary: `max_cb = max(k for k in cb if isinstance(k, int))` raises ValueError on an empty generator and exits with a traceback if no draw record carries cb_draws -- the shape a schema change or a dump from an older build would have.
scenario: A future build renames or drops the column, or someone runs the checker against a pre-schema-1 dump. Instead of 'this is not a frame dump I can read', the operator gets a Python traceback and no verdict. FDUMP_SCHEMA exists and is written into the header but the checker never reads it.
remediation: Guard the max() and report the missing column by name; read session['schema'] and refuse anything != 1 with a message rather than a traceback.
evidence: framedump_check.py:103-107; renderer.c:1529 (#define FDUMP_SCHEMA 1) and renderer.c:1745 (it is written into the session header).

summary: fdump_clear_previous(fdump.base) runs before the fopen at renderer.c:1712, so an arm that cannot open its output has already deleted the previous dump.
scenario: A second arm lands on a read-only or full path -- or the M1 directory after a first dump succeeded elsewhere. The previous run's dump is gone, the new one does not exist, and the FDUMP_LOG line reports only the fopen failure. The device is left with nothing.
remediation: Move the clear below the successful fopen. There is no collision risk in doing so: the session id is a timestamp, so the new file's name never matches an old one.
evidence: renderer.c:1696-1713 (clear at :1697, fopen at :1712, the failure return at :1713-1715); renderer.c:1614-1631 (fdump_clear_previous).

summary: The noimages spec comment reads 'records only, ~1 MB instead of ~1 MB per frame'. The second figure is meant to be the with-images size (~900 KB per frame on top of the records), so as written the sentence tells a reader the token changes nothing.
scenario: Not a defect in behaviour. Filed because the spec comment is the only documentation of the token an operator types into a marker file, and this is the token that decides whether a dump is ~1 MB or ~30 MB.
